reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 27 --verse 2.12.5: Sāyaṇa’s commentary on 2.12.5 holds the evidence verbatim (ellipses skip only the grammatical note on sa and his citation of 8.100.3): apaśyanto janāḥ … pṛcchanti (people not seeing him ask where he is), na kvacid asau tiṣṭhatīti manyamānāḥ … eṣa indro nāstīti (thinking he stays nowhere they say he is not), yadyapy asau viśeṣato ’smābhir na dṛśyate tathāpi astīti viśvāsaṃ kuruta (though not distinctly seen, trust that he is). The reading, doubters who not seeing him think him nowhere, and a bidding to trust that Indra is though not plainly seen, is his, without drift; the merging of the askers and the sayers follows his one subject janāḥ. Wilson’s ‘(in any one place)’ follows him. Plain: day.js shows every verse of 2.12 ends ‘He, O men, is Indra’, so ‘refrain names Indra to the people’ is the text’s own; ‘those who’ removes the doubled word; no four words of the key.
